about.title: Ione Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Ione is a small place. With about 7,000 residents spread along Rt 104, Preston Avenue, Shakeley Lane and W Main Street, a fatal crash is rarely an abstract statistic here — it is a neighbor, a coworker, someone from church. In 2025, public records show 10 injury collisions in Ione, 14 people hurt, and 1 life lost. Behind that single number is a family now facing funeral costs, missing income, and an empty chair. California law recognizes those losses. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, kept separate from any criminal case, and it belongs first to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. LawProactive does not practice law. We simply connect grieving Amador County families with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash happened on Rt 104. Does that change anything about a wrongful death claim in Ione?
items.answer: It can. Rt 104 is a state route, and if a claim involves the condition of the road or the conduct of a government entity, California requires a formal claim on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. That is one reason families in Ione should speak with an attorney sooner rather than later, even while still grieving.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from any prosecution by the Amador County District Attorney. A criminal conviction is not required to pursue the civil claim, and waiting for the criminal case to end could put the two-year deadline at risk.
